newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam ready for refinery, no word on partners.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam ready for refinery, no word on partners.

text.p: Vietnam said on Monday that a feasibility study for the country's first oil refinery was now ready for government approval, but there was no word on whether foreign investors were ready to join the project.

"The feasibility study...is complete and has been submitted to the government for approval, marking a major project to boost the development of Vietnam Petroleum Corporation (Petrovietnam)," the official Vietnam News Agency said.
The study, whose findings were not given, was undertaken by Petrovietnam and a clutch of foreign partners last year.

Industry sources said Petrovietnam was now trying to persuade those same partners to invest in the $1.2-1.4 billion Dung Quat project, which Hanoi is anxious to get under way this year, even if that meant going ahead on its own.
"If somebody withdraws from the contract, we can do it ourselves," a senior official at Petrovietnam told Reuters. "If all withdrew, we must do it ourselves."
The French oil firm Total SA withdrew from the 6.5-million-tonne-per-year refinery in 1995, branding it economically unviable.
The site chosen for the project, in the central province of Quang Ngai, is an undeveloped area 1,000 km (600 miles) north of the country's oilfields and chief consumption base.
The Petrovietnam official said talks with investors were focusing on financial incentives, particularly the question of what access they would have to Vietnam's retail market.
Petrovietnam and a consortium led by South Korea's LG Group each had a 30-percent stake in the feasibility study, with U.S. firm Stone & Webster taking a three percent share from LG Group.
Two Taiwanese firms, Chinese Petroleum Corp and Chinese Investment Development Corp, shared 10 percent.
Malaysia's state oil firm Petroliam Nasional Berhad (Petronas) split 30 percent equally with the U.S. refiner Conoco Inc, a unit of DuPont Co.
When they signed up for the study, the partners stressed that the share split did not necessarily reflect the split would apply to any eventual joint venture project.
Vietnam, on a drive to cut a growing oil products import bill, has set its sights on building a second refinery, possibly in the northern port town of Haiphong.
Vietnam News Agency quoted Petrovietnam General Director Ho Si Thoang as saying Dung Quat would meet only half of projected domestic demand of 10-12 million tonnes a year by 2000.
